portal.windowWarning: You opened the portal in an ordinary browser tab: extensions and the shared profile can read what you type. Open it from the tray (Open portal) or with

mode.notifyLong: Let it through with a notification

header.timerTip: The portal locks after the time set in Settings without use; tools with a grant keep working. Log out closes the vault. Unlocking is one touch.

welcome.pitch: Vaultgate sits between your AI tools and the internet. It fills in your keys only at the moment a request leaves, and only where you allow it.
welcome.tagline: Runs on your PC. Open source. No subscription.
welcome.how1: Your passkey is the key to the vault
welcome.how1Text: No password to remember and no recovery code to keep safe. A security key, your phone or this PC.
welcome.how2: Every tool gets a virtual key
welcome.how2Text: It works only on this PC and through Vaultgate. If it leaks, you revoke it in one click.
welcome.how3: What isn't allowed doesn't go through
welcome.how3Text: Every decision has a name and lands in your log. So does everything that was stopped.
welcome.keysTitle: How do you want to unlock your vault?
welcome.keysIntro: One touch opens it. No password to remember.
welcome.keyIntro: The tool gets a virtual key of its own. Your real secrets stay in the vault.
welcome.paired: {name} is paired and has its own virtual key.
welcome.manualHelp: For tools where you can only fill in a proxy address and an API key. You see the key once; it then lives in the tool's settings, only works through Vaultgate, and you can revoke it anytime.
welcome.doneTools: Connected with their own virtual key: {names}
welcome.doneNoTools: No tool connected yet. You can do that later under Virtual keys.
welcome.doneEncrypted: Everything is encrypted on this PC, also names and the log
welcome.nextSecretText: an API key, shown once and then never again
welcome.nextGrantText: or approve it from the tray on first use
welcome.twoKeysText: Then one lost key is not a lost vault.
welcome.vaultCreated: Vault created with your first key.

login.title: Sign in
login.passkeyText: Touch your passkey. It also opens the vault.
login.bootstrapText: No passkey is registered yet. Unlock with your passphrase to register one.
login.lost: Lost your passkeys and your passphrase?
login.startOver: Lost all your keys? Then you start over with a new vault; your secrets are still with their source.

unlock.title: The vault is locked
unlock.passkeyText: It locks itself after a while without use. Touch your passkey to open it again.
unlock.passphraseText: Or unlock with your passphrase (for example when your passkey has no PRF).

recovery.title: Your recovery code
recovery.text: Keep this code on paper or in another vault. You see it only now, once. If you lose your passkeys and your passphrase, only this code still opens the vault.
recovery.confirm: Type the last 4 characters to confirm

main.noPasskey: No passkey registered yet. Add one under Passkeys: without a passkey you cannot sign in later.
main.onePasskey: You have one passkey. Add a second one, so that a lost key is not lost access.

wizard.title: Getting started

next.passkey: Add your passkey: without one you cannot sign in later.
next.key: Create a virtual key for your tool (or pair it with the device flow).
next.secret: Add your first secret, with the domain it may go to.
next.grant: Let the tool make a first call (approve it in the tray), or add a grant.

wizard.checkIntro: Check, without a real call, which rule a call of this key with this secret would get:

result.granted: works: a call goes straight through
result.needs-approval: the first call asks for approval in the tray (or add a grant)
result.tool-key-revoked: this virtual key has been revoked
result.target-host-not-allowed: the domain is not on the secret's allowlist

audit.title: Activity
audit.introNone: Nothing waits for you. Every decision carries the name of the rule that made it.
audit.introOne: 1 thing waits for you. Every decision carries the name of the rule that made it.
audit.intro: {count} things wait for you. Every decision carries the name of the rule that made it.
audit.allowPlaceConfirm: Also fill in {secret} at {place}? Only do this if the service expects it there.
audit.pick: Pick a decision on the left to see why it was made.

keys.clients: Clients outside this PC (IP or subnet)
keys.configAnthropic: Claude Code and other Anthropic clients
keys.configForward: Any other API: a placeholder in a header, the virtual key separately
keys.reactivateConfirm: Reactivate {name}? Its key and grants work again.
keys.revokeConfirm: Revoke {name}? The tool cannot do anything until you reactivate it.
keys.dialogTitleMcp: Virtual key for an MCP server
keys.copiedNote: Copied. After 60 seconds Vaultgate clears the clipboard if the key is still on it. Edge may ask once to allow reading the clipboard. Windows clipboard history (Win+V) keeps its own copy.
keys.intro: Every tool gets its own virtual key. If a key leaks, revoke it; your real secrets stay the same.
keys.empty: No virtual keys yet. Create one, or pair a tool.
keys.waitingHelp: Type the code from your terminal into the pairing request before you allow it.
keys.rotateWarning: The old key stops working right away.
keys.rotatingHelp: Each time this tool asks for its key, Vaultgate gives it a token that works for 10 minutes and replaces its stored key with a new one. If an old copy is used, Vaultgate revokes the tool and tells you. It cannot stop a program that runs as you from asking for a token itself.
keys.manualHelp: This key stays the same until you rotate it: Vaultgate does not change it where you put it (an environment variable or a config file). Pair the tool with "login --name" so its key rotates by itself.
keys.reaskHelp: When the tool fetches a new token after this time, Vaultgate asks you to touch your passkey.
keys.pick: Pick a key on the left.
keys.created: set on {date}; shown once, never again

secrets.sensitiveHelp: Every approval, even a one-time one, asks you to touch your passkey.
secrets.saved: Secret saved. Its value is not shown again.
secrets.rotatePrompt: New value for {name}. Make it at the provider first, then paste it here.
secrets.intro: Your real keys and logins. Vaultgate fills them into a request as it leaves, only for the domains you allow.
secrets.footer: A value never leaves the vault, except into the request it is meant for. Lost track of one? Rotate it with a new value from the provider.
secrets.addIntro: Vaultgate encrypts it right away. After saving, nobody can read it back, not even you.
secrets.kindLoginNote: Login. Vaultgate fills in the username and password itself.
secrets.domainHelp: Only this domain gets the secret. Anything else is stopped.
secrets.never: Shown never again. To change it later, use Rotate.
secrets.clipboardNote: After pasting, clear your clipboard history (Win+V). Vaultgate never shows or returns the value.
secrets.rotateWarning: After pasting, clear your clipboard history (Win+V). The old value stops working right away.
secrets.editIntro: Everything except the value. For a new value, use Rotate.
secrets.empty: No secrets yet. Add your first one.
secrets.revokeGrants: Its grants go with it: {list}. The key itself still works at the provider: revoke it there too.
secrets.renameWarning: Tools that ask for {{secret:{old}}} must use the new name. Grants and routes move along.
secrets.learning: not yet known: the first allowed call sets it
secrets.placesHelp: Where the secret goes into a request. Another place is stopped; you can allow it from Activity (at most 3).
secrets.pick: Pick a secret on the left.
secrets.kindKeyNote: API key or token. Filled into requests to its domains, nowhere else.
secrets.touchGrant: only for a grant, not for every request
secrets.touchSensitive: every approval, even a one-time one

grants.intro: A grant lets one tool use one secret on one domain. You choose what happens on use, and for how long.
grants.footer: Without a grant, a call asks you in the tray; no answer means stopped (approval-timeout). Other stopped calls are in Activity, each with its rule.
grants.addIntro: One tool, one secret, one domain. Or skip this: the first call asks in the tray.
grants.validHelp: After that it rests; the next call asks you again.
grants.revokeConfirm: Delete this grant? {chain}. The next call of this combination asks you again in the tray.
grants.empty: No grants yet. The first call of a tool asks you in the tray.
grants.temporary: for now: {mode}; then the rule above applies again
grants.pick: Pick a grant on the left.
grants.noteRunning: Calls go through until {time}. After that the next call asks you again.
grants.noteAlways: No end. Delete it here when the tool no longer needs it.
grants.noteExpired: Expired: the next call asks you in the tray. Renew it to let calls through again.

device.enterCode: Type the code shown in {name}'s terminal to confirm this pairing.
device.rotated: rotated: enter the code to reconnect
device.noTouch: Not paired: your passkey was not touched.

passkeys.intro: The keys that open your vault. Keep at least two, so one lost key is not a lost vault.
passkeys.securityKeyHelp: the strongest: the key does not live in your PC
passkeys.phoneHelp: scan a QR code, confirm with your fingerprint
passkeys.thisPcHelp: quick, but on the same machine as your agents
passkeys.anotherHelp: your phone or a second security key
passkeys.nothingToKeep: No password, no recovery code on paper: nothing anyone can steal. If you lose all your keys, you start over; your secrets are still with their source.
passkeys.noPrf: signs in, but does not open the vault
passkeys.registered: Passkey added. It opens the vault.
passkeys.registeredNoPrf: Passkey added, but without PRF: it signs you in, the vault still opens with your other key.
passkeys.signInOnly: {count} without PRF only sign you in to review activity: they cannot open the vault.
passkeys.renamePrompt: A name for this passkey, so you know which key is which (for example "YubiKey keyring"). Empty: the kind.
passkeys.prfNote: Opens the vault: its PRF output unwraps the vault key. Without this key or another one like it, the vault stays closed.
passkeys.noPrfNote: Signs you in to review activity, but has no PRF: it cannot open the vault or decrypt a secret.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: How Vaultgate asks you, locks itself and listens. Changes take effect on the next request.
settings.listenersIntro: By default Vaultgate only listens on this PC. Add an address to let tools on other machines in, for example a VM.
settings.listenersWarning: Virtual keys and secrets travel in plain text across the local network, without TLS. Only listen on private, host-only or trusted network adapters.
settings.listenersHelp: A virtual key also has to allow the client: Virtual keys, Edit.
settings.routesIntro: A path on Vaultgate that forwards to a host, for tools that only take a base URL. The secret goes into the header you choose.
settings.quietHoursHelp: every call is stopped, without asking you
settings.quietIntro: During these hours Vaultgate stops every call (rule quiet-hours) and asks nothing in the tray. Local time; a window may cross midnight.
settings.quietHelp: Removing or changing a window asks for a touch of your passkey.
settings.notificationsHelp: for grants that notify; approvals in the tray still ask
settings.themeHelp: dark or light, for this browser
settings.deleteVaultHelp: Permanently deletes all secrets, tools, and passkeys. This cannot be undone.
settings.deleteVaultConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this vault?
settings.deleteVaultWarning: All secrets and virtual keys will be permanently deleted. You will start over with a new vault.
settings.vaultDeleted: Vault deleted. You can start over.

tls.title: Certificates
tls.subtitle: Roots that Node and Mozilla trust, and a renewed certificate under a known root, need nothing from you. A new root you do not trust stops every request until you decide here.
tls.emptyTrusted: The roots that Node and Mozilla trust need nothing from you; they are not listed here.
tls.introDesc: Vaultgate guarantees that secrets only travel across verified connections. When a certificate is untrusted or modified, requests stop immediately.
tls.step1Desc: Identify who issued the certificate. Look up the name online or verify it with your company's IT support if you don't recognize it.
tls.step2Desc: Trust it only if it belongs to your organization's inspection proxy (e.g. Zscaler, Fortinet) or your own developer tools (e.g. mkcert, Fiddler). If the source is unknown, never trust it.
tls.inspectionWarn: When you trust a certificate root, the software or entity behind that certificate can read and inspect all your decrypted network traffic, including API requests and responses.
tls.trustWarn: Trusting this root allows {root} to decrypt and read all network traffic and secrets sent through it.
tls.trustInstruction: Only trust this root if you recognize it as your company's network security proxy or your own tool. Compare the fingerprint with IT or look up the issuer name.
tls.scopeHostDesc: Least privilege. Other domains will still ask if they use this root.
tls.scopeGlobalDesc: Recommended for Zscaler/Fortinet. Requests will show an orange inspected badge in Activity.
tls.untrustDesc: Requests through {root} are stopped again, with tls-untrusted.
tls.untrustImmediate: Restricting trust takes effect immediately and does not require a touch.
tls.reviewRootsDesc: Roots in the Windows store that Node and Mozilla do not trust. Vaultgate trusts none of them unless you say so.
tls.text: Before: {before} · now: {now}. No secret goes there until you trust the new chain. If you did not expect this (for example on another network), do not trust it.
tls.textUntrusted: Issuer now: {now} · root: {root} · valid to: {validTo}. This root is not trusted yet; no secret goes there until you trust it.
tls.globalNote: It can read what passes through it. Every request it handles shows "inspected" in Activity.
tls.hostNote: Only for {origin}. Any other domain that ends at this root is stopped.
tls.changedNote: The chain of {host} now ends at {root}, a root you do not trust. A man in the middle looks exactly like this. Nothing went out: secrets stayed in the vault.
tls.untrustedNote: {host} ends at {root}, a root you do not trust. Nothing went out: secrets stayed in the vault.
tls.notYours: Not your company proxy? Keep blocking: do nothing.

waiting.title: Waiting for you
waiting.approval: {tool} asks for {secret} on {host}: answer in the tray

rollback.title: This is an older copy of the vault
rollback.text: The vault in this folder is older than the last one opened on this PC. That happens when a backup is restored, but also when someone puts back an old copy to bring back a revoked tool or a removed grant. The vault stays closed until you confirm.
rollback.accept: I restored this backup on purpose: open it anyway

integrity.title: Vaultgate's own files changed
integrity.text: These files of Vaultgate are not the same as when the vault was last opened here. That happens after an update, but also when a program changes Vaultgate, for example so that the tray always answers "allow". The vault stays closed until you confirm.
integrity.accept: I updated or changed Vaultgate myself: open the vault anyway

specs.title: Security
specs.help: The key hierarchy, the encryption and its parameters, explained on the website.

mcpInstall.help: Put Vaultgate in your agents on this PC with one click. The agent gets the tool's name, never the key; restart the agent afterwards.
mcpInstall.none: No agents found on this PC.
mcpInstall.skillHelp: Copies SKILL.md and sets the core policy rule for Claude, Copilot and other agents.
mcpInstall.refreshNothing: Everything is up to date; no file changed.

touch.title: Touch your passkey
touch.why: A program can click buttons. It cannot touch your passkey.
touch.gone: This question no longer exists (expired or already answered).

question.sensitive: {tool} wants to use the sensitive secret {secret} on {host}.
question.device: {tool} wants to be paired and get its own key.
question.reask: {tool} wants a new token. You asked Vaultgate to check with you every few hours.

touch.denied: Denied. You can close this window.
touch.confirmed: Confirmed. You can close this window.
touch.failed: Not confirmed: no valid touch. The question was denied.
touch.codeHint: Code {code} matches your terminal. Touch your passkey to confirm.
touch.closeHint: Window still open? Close it with Alt+F4.

rules.approved-always: {tool} used {secret} on {host}; you allowed it from now on.
rules.target-host-not-allowed: {tool} wanted to send {secret} to {host}. Stopped; nothing was decrypted.
rules.no-tool-key: A call without a valid virtual key. Stopped.
rules.client-not-allowed: {tool} called from a machine that is not allowed. Stopped.
rules.no-placeholder: {tool} made a call without a secret placeholder. Stopped.
rules.unknown-secret: {tool} asked for {secret}, which does not exist. Stopped.
rules.placeholder-location-not-allowed: {tool} put {secret} where it may not go. Stopped.
rules.bad-target: {tool} asked for {secret} on {host} with an encoded character in the path (such as %2f), which could slip past the allowed path. Stopped; nothing was decrypted.
rules.grant-expired: The grant of {tool} for {secret} has expired; asked again.
rules.approval-timeout: Nobody answered in time for {tool} → {secret} → {host}. Denied.
rules.approval-unavailable: {tool} needed an approval, but the tray was not running. Denied.
rules.touch-denied: Your passkey was not touched for {tool} → {secret}. Denied.
rules.touch-timeout: No passkey touch in time for {tool} → {secret}. Denied.
rules.vault-locked: The vault was locked; nothing was decrypted.
rules.throttled: Too many wrong attempts; this caller waits before it gets an answer.
rules.tls-chain-changed: Another certificate chain for {host}. Nothing is sent until you decide.
rules.tls-chain-accepted: You trusted the new certificate chain for {host}.
rules.audit-unavailable: The log could not be written, so nothing was sent.
rules.device-name-taken: {tool} asked for a name that already exists. Refused.
rules.tunnel-not-supported: A tunnel to {host} was refused: Vaultgate cannot fill in or check it.
rules.response-scrubbed: {host} sent {secret} back in its response; Vaultgate removed it before {tool} saw it.
rules.subdomain-denied: {tool} asked for {secret} on {host}, a new subdomain; it was not added. Stopped; nothing was decrypted.
rules.secret-places-changed: Where {secret} may be filled in was changed.
rules.secret-removed: Secret {secret} was deleted, with its grants.
rules.tool-renamed: A virtual key was renamed to {tool}.
rules.tool-clients-changed: The machines that may use {tool} were changed.
rules.tool-key-rotated: {tool} got a new key; the old one stopped working.
rules.tool-key-repaired: {tool} was paired again and got a new key.
rules.tool-removed: Virtual key {tool} was deleted, with its grants.
rules.grant-changed: The grant of {tool} for {secret} on {host} was changed.
rules.new-passkey-added: A passkey was added to the vault.
rules.passkey-renamed: A passkey got a new name.
rules.passkey-removed: A passkey was removed from the vault.
rules.passkey-prf-enrolled: A passkey can now open the vault.
rules.step-up-confirmed: A change was confirmed with a touch of your passkey.
rules.vault-recovered: The vault was recovered with the recovery code; there is a new passphrase.
rules.grant-blocked: The grant of {tool} for {secret} on {host} was blocked.
rules.grant-unblocked: The grant of {tool} for {secret} on {host} was unblocked.
rules.grant-notifications-snoozed: Notifications for one grant were snoozed.
rules.tls-untrusted-accepted: You trusted the certificate root for {host}.
rules.quiet-hours: {tool} asked for {secret} on {host} during quiet hours. Stopped; nothing was decrypted.
rules.grant-notifications-resumed: Notifications for one grant are on again.

errors.DEVICE_CODE_INVALID: The pairing code is not right. Check the code in your terminal and type it again.
errors.WRONG_CREDENTIALS: That did not open the vault.
errors.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.VAULT_EXISTS: There is already a vault here.
errors.PRF_REQUIRED: This key cannot open the vault (it has no PRF). Use a security key, your phone or Windows Hello.
errors.WEBAUTHN_FAILED: The passkey could not be verified. Try again.
errors.PASSKEY_CREATE_FAILED: Creating the passkey did not finish (stopped after {seconds} s). On a phone: scan the QR code, then save the passkey in the app the phone offers. Try again, or choose another key.
errors.PASSKEY_PRF_FAILED: The passkey was created, but reading its vault key did not finish (stopped after {seconds} s). Your phone or app may not support the PRF extension that Vaultgate needs to open the vault. Try a security key or this PC.
errors.VAULT_ROLLED_BACK: This is an older copy of the vault. Confirm in the warning below if you restored it on purpose.
errors.CODE_CHANGED: Vaultgate's own files changed. Confirm in the warning below if you updated or changed it yourself.
errors.STEP_UP_REQUIRED: Touch your passkey to confirm this change. Nothing was changed.
errors.STEP_UP_CANCELLED: Confirming with a touch did not finish. Nothing was changed.
errors.STEP_UP_UNAVAILABLE: No passkey can confirm this change (blocked, or not allowed by the touch setting). Nothing was changed.
errors.LAST_PASSKEY: Keep at least one passkey that is not blocked.
errors.INVALID_QUIET_HOURS: Use windows like 23:00-07:00 (24 h), one per line.
